y2-12.recommendedPriorKnowledge: De cursus Neuroanatomie en neurofysiologie (5102VNAN9Y) geldt als aanbevolen voorkennis. Tijdens het fysiologiepracticum van de cursus Neuroanatomie en neurofysiologie heb je twee computermodellen (Membraanpotentiaal en Actiepotentiaal) gebruikt om een aantal passieve en actieve elektrofysiologische eigenschappen van prikkelbare cellen te bestuderen. De informatie uit die practica, maar ook de eerder behandelde theorie uit deze cursus, wordt als bekend verondersteld.

components: The mathematics course assumes pre-university Mathematics A knowledge; students with Mathematics A start its preparatory teaching earlier than students with Mathematics B.
Academic Basic Skills 1.2 requires completion of 1.1. Both are completed in the first year.

Second-year courses require at least 42 EC from Year 1. The experimental courses additionally require both Academic Basic Skills courses and Research Methods and Statistics; the review additionally requires both Academic Basic Skills courses. This pathway completes all 60 first-year credits first.
Philosophy of Science and Statistical Reasoning
The programming practical is completed before Experimental Psychology, as strongly recommended. Experimental Psychology and programming precede the EEG practical.
The second-year review is a literature study with an English report and presentation. It is a separate prerequisite for the later bachelor project.
Experimentation — Neurophysiology is the current name of the former Hodgkin & Huxley and Neuropharmacology practical; both names refer to the same requirement.

Thirty EC remain open for approved electives, a minor or exchange. No particular course or host is assumed. At most 12 EC of the elective space may be introductory first-year courses; outside courses require advance approval and must avoid excessive overlap. All first-year courses must be passed before third-year programme electives.

This example selects the permitted extended 30-EC scientific internship/project. Entry requires 120 EC one month before starting, including the full first year, Philosophy of Science and Statistical Reasoning, the second-year review and all five experimental practicals: programming, experimental psychology, EEG, molecular cell biology and neurophysiology. Completing both earlier years meets these conditions. The project includes supervised original research, an English scientific report and an English presentation; no host or research topic is assumed.
findings: Current programme and dated guide confirm biological explanations of brain, cognition, emotion and behaviour, integrated with psychology and experimental research. Years 1 and 2 each have sixty compulsory EC. There is no mandatory formal track to select. Cognitive, molecular and evolutionary emphases are optional packages, not additional degree components.

The guide’s project entry shows the mandatory eighteen-credit base; its own contents expressly permit eighteen, twenty-four or thirty EC. The choice page permits using six or twelve credits of the forty-two-credit open window to extend the project. Retained the thirty-credit project plus thirty genuinely open elective credits. No project base is counted twice, no named elective is invented, and the misleading guide aggregate forty-eight for Year 3 is not used as a degree total.

Academic Basic Skills 1.2 requires 1.1 and follows it in Year 1. Later second-year courses require forty-two first-year EC. Experimental practicals additionally require both skills courses and Research Methods/Statistics; the review requires both skills courses. Completing all sixty first-year EC meets these conditions and the forty-two-credit BSA. Genetics precedes Cell Biology and Evolution/Behaviour; earlier cellular/neural foundations supply recommended knowledge for Neuroanatomy/Physiology.

Programming, Experimental Psychology and EEG have period offerings allowing the recommended sequence: programming in period two, experimental psychology in period three, EEG in period four. The final two practicals run in period five. Science/statistical reasoning and the review are also completed before project entry. Experimentation—Neurophysiology is the renamed Hodgkin & Huxley/Neuropharmacology practical; the transition page confirms this alias rather than a new extra requirement.

Project entry is checked one month before starting: 120 degree EC including all sixty Year-1 EC, Philosophy of Science/Statistical Reasoning, the Year-2 review and the five named experimental practicals. The study/career-orientation module is not one of those five practicals. Completing both prior years satisfies every requirement before the Year-3 project. The project has supervised original empirical research, data analysis, an English scientific report and English presentation; its host and subject remain open.

The thirty remaining elective EC are genuinely open to programme electives, outside electives, an approved minor or exchange. All first-year courses must be passed before programme Year-3 electives, outside courses require prior approval and must not overlap excessively, and at most twelve EC may be introductory. These conditions are retained without constructing an unevidenced package. No additional OER is imposed because dated programme and course entries establish the relevant rules without a material unresolved conflict.

Course content was read for all twenty-three compulsory taught units and the project. Development includes embryology/molecular neurodevelopment as well as cognitive/social development; Learning/Memory includes cellular and neural mechanisms; the review is a literature study. EEG requires actual recording and analysis, while Neurophysiology combines Hodgkin/Huxley simulations with axon experiments. These distinctions limit UCR claims. No meta-analysis course is treated as the mandatory internship.
